On Mon, Apr 19, 2027 at 09:18 AM Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.example> wrote:
> David — thanks, and great detail.

Adding a few technical notes to make sure the simulations match our runtime behavior:
- Caching model: we simulate prefix/KV cache hit rates at route-level. For user-specific history we treat the KV cache as partially effective — identical prefix hits provide >90% savings on tokenized model compute but only if the cache window is warm.
- Batching behavior: continuous batching yields two levers — increased GPU utilization (cost down) vs. added per-request latency. For UI routes we cap batching to 4–8 inputs; for async flows we use 16+.
- Long-tail tokens: for sequences >1024 tokens we route to a larger memory profile and disable aggressive batching to protect p99. That changes tokens/$ by ~40% for those requests.

For the sim: provide us a small sample of request histograms if you can (sequence length distribution + percent identical prompts). If not, we’ll run the 10/30/60 hit-rate sims Priyom suggested.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: MAP + token sensitivity sims attached — key takeaways and gating

David — attaching the draft and the sim outputs per plan. TL;DR upfront, then bullets:

TL;DR:
- Under Greenfield baseline (no cache, batch=1): ~0.0019 tokens/$ (i.e., $525 per million tokens) — this is our conservative hosted price-equivalent for your traffic shape.
- With modest caching (30% prefix hit) + batching (batch=4), effective tokens/$ improves to ~0.0048 tokens/$ (roughly $210 per million tokens) — 60% improvement on unit cost.
- If you can reach 60% caching on repeated system prompts and allow async batching for lower-priority routes, unit costs can approach ~0.009 tokens/$ (~$110 per million tokens).

Key assumptions used in sims (highlighted in the attached CSV):
- Request profile: median request 120 tokens in, 220 tokens out (as you provided), with a 5% long-tail >1024 tokens.
- Cache hit scenarios modeled: 10% / 30% / 60% prefix hits. Hits are applied only to non-authenticated shared prompts unless explicitly flagged as user-shared.
- Batching options: 1, 4, 16. Batching improves GPU utilization linearly up to batch=8 then shows diminishing returns.
- SLA constraints: for UI-critical routes we assume p99 latency budget of 200ms; batch=4 is our recommended sweet spot. For background/async routes aim for batch=16.

Gating and acceptance criteria for pilot (MAP):
- Unit cost target for pilot signoff: <= $250 per million tokens (approx tokens/$ >= 0.004).
- Perf: UI routes p99 <= 220ms and error rate < 0.5% under peak profile.
- Quality: >= baseline accuracy on the 5 eval prompts bundle we discussed (attached to the MAP).

Edge cases and recommended mitigations:
- Cache pollution from authenticated history: recommend per-customer sliding window cache and TTLs (default 30 minutes) to limit pollution.
- Long-sequence fallback: route >1024 tokens to reserved nodes with lower batching and flag for cost monitoring.
- Burst protection: use conservative autoscale buffer + a fallback model variant with lower-cost tokens/$ to preserve availability.

Next steps:
1) David: confirm whether finance is comfortable with the pilot cost gate of $250/M tokens or wants a stricter target.
2) Greenfield: share a small sample histogram (even 1k rows) to replace our assumed distribution — that will tighten sims.
3) Redwood: we’ll prepare a condensed MAP slide for your exec review and a short runbook for the pilot (deployment config + gating checks).

Attachments: Greenfield_MAP_v0.9.xlsx, token_simulations_q2.csv
